guard: Windows detached up requests job breakaway safely, returns a signalable active child contract, and applies one errno-dependent pid ownership rule at every cleanup site
why: The pure decision seam deterministically covers Windows job states on every CI platform; the native branch still runs in the Windows workflow.
The child contract is exercised with injected signalling functions, so no real process is spawned or killed on a non-Windows host.

One ownership rule governs every cleanup wrapper: a returned kill result, including normalized ESRCH false, permits stale pid removal; EPERM or any other throw preserves the pidfile because death was not established.

Cell map used by every mechanical derivation: C01 outside-job detach; C02 allowed-job breakaway; C03 hostile-job refusal; C04 exact pid and signal; C05 already-gone false; C06 active null state; C07 unobservable exit fails loud; C08 unbound EPERM keeps pid; C09 unbound preserves primary and cause; C10 unbound ESRCH removes stale pid; C11 not-ready EPERM keeps pid; C12 not-ready preserves primary and cause; C13 not-ready ESRCH removes stale pid; C14 postStart EPERM keeps pid; C15 postStart preserves primary and cause; C16 postStart ESRCH removes stale pid.

Each mutation note lists every IN cell that reads the changed behavior and groups every OUT cell with the reason it does not. This derivation is written before the mutation run and is checked against the observed mark delta afterward.

UNEXERCISED PRODUCTION BOUNDARY: windowsDetachedChild using its default signalProcess = process.kill is not run here. Tests inject signal functions and therefore prove the shaped-handle contract, not the native process signal.
UNEXERCISED PRODUCTION BOUNDARY: nativeWindowsLauncher.spawn returning windowsDetachedChild after the real PowerShell and CreateProcess path is not run here.

UNEXERCISED NATIVE DETAILS: Windows argument quoting, environment block construction, durable log handle wiring, job probe, CreateProcess flags, and pid parsing remain covered only by source review and the Windows workflow, not this cross-platform smoke.

HELD DESIGN BLOCKER: the native launcher closes pi.hProcess and returns a bare pid, so this smoke does not prove process identity remains pinned across pid reuse. That design decision is explicitly outside this fold.
